**Transportation Model**

Let  

- \(I\) be the set of Walmart stores (indexed by \(i\)).  
- \(J\) be the set of customer groups (indexed by \(j\)).  

Parameters  

- \(s_i\) : daily supply capacity of store \(i\)  \((i \in I)\).  
- \(d_j\) : daily demand of customer group \(j\)  \((j \in J)\).  
- \(c_{ij}\) : transportation cost per unit from store \(i\) to customer \(j\)  \((i \in I,\; j \in J)\).  

Decision variables  

- \(x_{ij} \ge 0\) : quantity shipped from store \(i\) to customer \(j\)  \((i \in I,\; j \in J)\).  

**Model**

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{j \in J} c_{ij}\,x_{ij} \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.}\quad
& \sum_{j \in J} x_{ij} \;\le\; s_i, && \forall i \in I \quad \text{(supply limits)}\\[4pt]
& \sum_{i \in I} x_{ij} \;=\; d_j, && \forall j \in J \quad \text{(demand satisfaction)}\\[4pt]
& x_{ij} \;\ge\; 0, && \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
\end{aligned}
\]

This linear programming formulation minimizes total transportation cost while ensuring that each store’s supply capacity is not exceeded and every customer group’s demand is met exactly.

     [1791.49, 68.21, 1432.48, 1527.76]]

m.optimize()

for i in I:
